title: Cauliflower “Steak”
notes: Rejuvelac. Rejuvelac is a fermented grain or seed liquid high in probiotics and is used both in vegan cheese making and as a probiotic supplement. It should taste like tangy lemonade; a bit sweet, slightly tart, but not sour. Be sure to follow safe food practices when fermenting food.

ingredientSections.heading: Cauliflower
items: Pumpkin or sunflower seeds to garnish

ingredientSections.heading: Rejuvelac
items: ½ Cup whole wheat, rye or quinoa (each will have different flavours)

methodSections.heading: Tabbouleh
steps: Cook the quinoa and allow to cool, the cooked weight should be around 500g. Mince the mint, halve the tomatoes, chop the parsley, finely dice the lemon and onion and medium dice the cucumber.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl and mix well.

methodSections.heading: Cauliflower
steps: Chop the tomatoes, place in a bowl and stir in the salt. Slice the onion and mince the garlic, set aside.
Bring the oil to a high temperature in a saucepan. Add the onions and garlic and cook until translucent. Add the spices and toast until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the harissa paste, lemon juice and sugar. Drain the tomatoes, add to the saucepan and cook until the liquid has reduced by half. Blend until smooth.
Cut one cauliflower steak from the middle of each cauliflower and save the remainder for another recipe, for example see page 204. Score the steaks with shallow cross cuts to assist the marinade.
Rub the marinade onto the cauliflower, place on an oven tray or dish and roast in the oven at 190°C (375°F) for 20-25 minutes or until golden and tender.
Serve on top of the tabbouleh, nut feta and cilantro cream (over page) and drizzled with tamarind purée. Garnish with a sprinkle of pumpkin or sunflower seeds and serve with a charred half lemon.

methodSections.heading: Tamarind Purée
steps: Soak the tamarind paste in 500ml hot water and set aside. Slice the onions finely.
Caramelize the sugar in 15ml (1 Tbsp) of water in saucepan over high heat. Watch very closely as the sugar will go from caramelized to burnt very quickly.
Add the onions to the caramelized sugar and stir well to combine. Cook until the onions are caramelized, stirring often to prevent sticking and scorching.
Remove the seeds from the tamarind paste by passing through a sieve or squeezing with your hands. Stir into the caramelized onions.
Add the red wine vinegar, raisins and agave syrup. Cook until 80 per cent of the liquid has cooked off and a jam-like consistency is achieved.

methodSections.heading: Almond Feta
steps: Soak almonds overnight, drain and rinse. Blend with the rejuvelac or sauerkraut liquid and the salt until as smooth as possible.
Cover with plastic wrap or a tight lid and let sit at room temperature for 1-2 days to culture. Taste regularly, a pleasant tanginess will develop.
To solidify, bring a ½ cup of water to a boil in a small saucepan. Stir through the agar agar, cover and simmer for 5 minutes.

Line an appropriately sized mould or moulds with cheesecloth. Stir the cultured almond mixture and agar liquid together thoroughly then pour into the mould. Place in the fridge to set which will take a couple of hours. The flavours will develop even further with time.

methodSections.heading: Creamy Cilantro
steps: Soak the almonds overnight.
Drain and rinse almonds before blending with the water and rice wine vinegar until completely smooth.
Add the remaining ingredients and, again, blend until smooth.
For a simpler version of this dish, you could skip this element and simply garnish with a few sprigs of fresh cilantro.

methodSections.heading: Rejuvelac
steps: Follow steps 1 to 3 in the section “Sprouting Seeds and Grains”.
Place the sprouts back in the jar and fill with water. Cover and set aside covered for 2 days, stirring occasionally.
The resulting liquid is the first batch of rejuvelac, strain this into a bottle and store in the fridge for up to 7 days.
Fill the sprouts jar with water again and repeat the process with the same sprouts for a second batch.
